title: Explicit three-arrow adjunction exchange diagram
statement: A three-arrow diagram in a category retains four objects and its three morphisms. Its composite is first followed by second followed by third. A functor maps every object and arrow and preserves this composite. For adjunctions U left adjoint R and V left adjoint S, functors G and H, and a transformation G V to U H, the exchange diagram at K has vertices G R K, S V G R K, S H U R K, S H K, and arrows the unit, S applied to the square component, and S H applied to the counit. Its composite equals the actual Mathlib mate component. The endpoint-typed mapHom is exactly F.map and sends the original composite to the mapped diagram composite, retaining the mapped diagram endpoint expressions in its return type.

proof.text: Construct the four vertices and arrows directly. Map all fields by the given functor; map_comp twice proves preservation of the composite. Expand mateEquiv at an object, functor composition, whiskering and unitors to obtain exactly the three specified arrows. The construction works in every category, including empty and zero categories. Give mapHom the mapped diagram endpoints explicitly and define it to be F.map; reflexivity proves mapHom_eq, and map_composite proves mapHom_composite.
